extracted.intended_audience: Issuers, filing persons, corporate counsel, and other professionals preparing SEC tender offer, going-private, and asset-backed securities (Regulation M-A and Regulation AB) filings
extracted.subtask_description: Regulation M-A disclosure requirements for tender offers and going-private (Items 1011–1016) and the opening provisions of Regulation AB (Items 1100–1101) governing presentation of historical performance, third-party information, participants, foreign considerations, exhibits, and definitions for asset-backed securities filings. Used by filers and their advisors to prepare required SEC schedules, prospectuses and exhibits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 1011(a) Agreements, regulatory requirements and legal proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: If material to a security holder's decision whether to sell, tender or hold the securities sought in the tender offer, furnish: (1) any present or proposed material agreement, arrangement, understanding or relationship between the offeror (or its executive officers, directors, controlling persons or subsidiaries) and the subject company (or its executive officers, directors, controlling persons or subsidiaries) (other than items disclosed elsewhere in Regulation M-A); (2) the applicable regulatory requirements which must be complied with or approvals which must be obtained in connection with the tender offer (to the extent known after reasonable investigation); (3) the applicability of any anti-trust laws; (4) the applicability of margin requirements under section 7 of the Act and the applicable regulations; and (5) any material pending legal proceedings relating to the tender offer, including court/agency name and location, date instituted, principal parties, a brief summary of the proceedings and the relief sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction: In an issuer tender offer disclose any material agreement/relationship between the offeror and its executive officers, directors, controlling persons or subsidiaries. Instruction to (a)(5): A copy of any document relating to a major development in a material pending legal proceeding (e.g., pleadings, answers, complaints, TROs, injunctions, opinions, judgments or orders) must be furnished promptly to the Commission staff on a supplemental basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 1011(b) Executive officer compensation related to the transaction (Item 402(t) disclosure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Furnish the information required by Item 402(t)(2) and (3) and in the tabular format set forth in Item 402(t)(1) with respect to each named executive officer: (1) of the subject company in a Rule 13e-3 transaction; or (2) of the issuer whose securities are the subject of a third-party tender offer, regarding any agreement or understanding (written or unwritten) between such named executive officer and the subject company, issuer, bidder, or acquiring company concerning any type of compensation (present, deferred or contingent) that is based upon or otherwise relates to the Rule 13e-3 transaction or third-party tender offer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructions: Obligation does not apply where the issuer is a foreign private issuer or an emerging growth company. Quantify disclosure assuming the triggering event on the latest practicable date and determine price per share as: fixed dollar amount if fixed, otherwise average closing market price over the first five business days following the first public announcement. Compute dollar value of in-the-money option awards by difference between this price and exercise/base price. Include only compensation based on or relating to the subject transaction. Apply the instruction with respect to those executive officers for whom disclosure was required in the most recent applicable filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 1011(c) Other material information
rubrics_metrics.description: Furnish such additional material information, if any, as may be necessary to make the required statements, in light of the circumstances under which they are made, not materially misleading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 1012 Solicitation or recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: State the nature of the solicitation or the recommendation. If a recommendation, state whether the filing person is advising holders to accept or reject the tender offer or to take other action and describe the other action. If the subject company is not making a recommendation, state whether it is expressing no opinion, remaining neutral, or is unable to take a position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also: (b) Reasons — state the reasons for the position; conclusory statements (e.g., 'in the best interests of shareholders') are insufficient. (c) Intent to tender — to the extent known after reasonable inquiry, state whether the filing person or any executive officer, director, affiliate or subsidiary currently intends to tender, sell or hold subject securities held of record or beneficially. (d) Intent to tender or vote in a going-private transaction — state whether any executive officer, director or affiliate currently intends to tender/sell or how they intend to vote subject securities (including proxies) and state reasons; if unavailable at initial filing, file promptly and in no event later than three business days after initial filing, and if material, disclose in a manner reasonably designed to inform security holders. (e) Recommendations of others — state whether persons specified in (d) have made recommendations in support or opposition and the reasons for those recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 1013 Purposes, alternatives, reasons and effects in a going-private transaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Require disclosure of: (a) the purposes for the Rule 13e-3 transaction; (b) if alternatives were considered to accomplish the stated purposes, briefly describe the alternatives and reasons for their rejection; (c) the reasons for the structure of the transaction and for undertaking it at this time; and (d) the effects of the Rule 13e-3 transaction on the subject company, its affiliates and unaffiliated security holders, including the federal tax consequences of the transaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructions: (1) Conclusory statements insufficient. (2) The description of effects must include a reasonably detailed discussion of both benefits and detriments and must quantify benefits and detriments to the extent practicable. (3) If the statement is filed by an affiliate, include the effect of the transaction on the affiliate's interest in net book value and net earnings in both dollar amounts and percentages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 1014 Fairness of the going-private transaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Require disclosure of: (a) whether the subject company or affiliate reasonably believes the Rule 13e-3 transaction is fair or unfair to unaffiliated security holders and identification of any director who dissented or abstained (with reasons, if known); (b) a discussion in reasonable detail of the material factors upon which the fairness belief is based and the weight assigned to each factor (including analysis of the extent beliefs are based on the factors in paragraphs (c),(d),(e) and Item 1015); (c) whether approval of at least a majority of unaffiliated security holders is required; (d) whether a majority of non-employee directors has retained an unaffiliated representative to act solely on behalf of unaffiliated security holders; (e) whether the transaction was approved by a majority of non-employee directors; and (f) if any offers of certain types were received, describe the offer and reasons for its rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructions: (1) A statement that the issuer or affiliate has no reasonable belief as to fairness is not sufficient. (2) Factors important in determining fairness vary but normally include: (i) current market prices; (ii) historical market prices; (iii) net book value; (iv) going concern value; (v) liquidation value; (vi) prior purchase prices disclosed under Item 1002(f); (vii) any report/opinion/appraisal described in Item 1015; and (viii) firm offers known to the subject company in the past two years for merger/sale/purchase enabling control. (3) Conclusory statements (e.g., 'the transaction is fair') are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 1015 Reports, opinions, appraisals and negotiations
rubrics_metrics.description: Require disclosure of: (a) whether the subject company or affiliate has received any report, opinion (other than counsel opinion) or appraisal from an outside party materially related to the Rule 13e-3 transaction; and (b) for each such report/opinion/appraisal or negotiation/report described in Item 1014(d) or Schedule 14A Item 14(b)(6): (1) identify the outside party/unaffiliated representative; (2) briefly describe qualifications of the party/representative; (3) describe the method of selection; (4) describe any material relationship during the past two years (or contemplated) and any compensation received or to be received by the outside party/affiliates in relation to the subject company or its affiliates; (5) state whether the subject company determined the amount of consideration or whether the outside party recommended the amount; and (6) furnish a summary of the negotiation/report including procedures followed, findings/recommendations, bases/methods used, instructions received from the subject company or affiliate, and any limitation imposed on scope of investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction: Information required by paragraphs (b)(1),(2) and (3) must be given with respect to the firm that provides the report/opinion/appraisal rather than individual employees. (c) Furnish a statement that the report/opinion/appraisal will be made available for inspection and copying at the principal executive offices during regular business hours by any interested equity security holder or designated representative and that a copy will be transmitted upon written request at the expense of the requesting security holder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 1016 Exhibits
rubrics_metrics.description: File as exhibits to the schedule: (a) any disclosure materials furnished to security holders by or on behalf of the filing person including tender offer materials (including transmittal letter), solicitation or recommendation (including Item 1012 materials), going-private disclosure document, prospectus used in connection with an exchange offer where securities are registered under the Securities Act, and any other disclosure materials; (b) any loan agreement referred to in response to Item 1007(d); (c) any report, opinion or appraisal referred to in Item 1014(d) or Item 1015; (d) any document setting forth the terms of any agreement, arrangement or understanding referred to in Item 1005(e) or Item 1011(a)(1); (e) any agreement or pertinent portions of any proxy statement, report or other communication containing disclosure required by Item 1005(d); (f) a detailed statement describing security holders' appraisal rights and procedures referred to in Item 1004(d); (g) any written instruction, form or other material furnished to persons making oral solicitations or recommendations; and (h) any written tax opinion prepared by legal counsel at the filing person's request and communicated to the filing person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhibit Table maps which items require which exhibits (e.g., Disclosure Material, Loan Agreement, Report/Opinion/Appraisal, Contracts/Arrangements, Statement re: Appraisal Rights, Oral Solicitation Materials, Tax Opinion). Instructions: (1) Schedules/attachments to exhibits not required to be filed if they do not contain information material to an investment or voting decision and that information is not otherwise disclosed in the exhibit or disclosure document; each exhibit must contain a list briefly identifying contents of omitted schedules and the registrant must provide a copy of omitted schedule to the Commission or staff upon request. (2) Registrant may redact information from exhibits if disclosure would constitute a clearly unwarranted invasion of personal privacy (e.g., bank account numbers, social security numbers, home addresses); a list of omitted information suffices if already included within the exhibit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 1100(a) Application of Regulation AB
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulation AB (§§ 229.1100 through 229.1125) is the source of various disclosure items and requirements for 'asset-backed securities' filings under the Securities Act and the Exchange Act; definitions used in Regulation AB, including 'asset-backed security,' are set forth in Item 1101.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 1100(b) Presentation of historical delinquency and loss information
rubrics_metrics.description: Several Items in Regulation AB call for presentation of historical information and data on delinquencies and loss information. Present delinquency experience in 30- or 31-day increments beginning at least with assets that are 30 or 31 days delinquent through the point assets are written off or charged off as uncollectible; at minimum present by number of accounts and dollar amount. Present statistical information in tabular or graphical format if such presentation will aid understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also: (2) disclose total amount of delinquent assets as a percentage of the aggregate asset pool; (3) present loss and cumulative loss information regarding charge-offs, charge-off rate, gross losses, recoveries and net losses (with description of how terms are defined), the number and amount of assets experiencing a loss and number/amount with a recovery, the ratio of aggregate net losses to average portfolio balance, and the average of net loss on all assets that experienced a net loss; (4) categorize delinquency and loss information by pool asset type; (5) in a registration statement or prospectus describe how delinquencies, charge-offs and uncollectible accounts are defined/determined addressing effect of grace periods, re-aging, restructures, partial payments considered current or other practices; (6) describe other material information particular to pool asset type (e.g., repossession, foreclosure, REO).

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 1100(c) Presentation of certain third party information (incorporation by reference and reference information)
rubrics_metrics.description: If information of a third party is required by certain Regulation AB items (e.g., Item 1112(b), Items 1114(b)(2) or 1115(b), or Item 1125), such information may, in lieu of including it, be provided by incorporation by reference to reports filed by the third party under Exchange Act section 13(a) or 15(d), provided specified conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions for incorporation by reference include: (i) the third party (or consolidating entity) is required to file reports under section 13(a) or 15(d); (ii) the third party has filed all required reports and materials during the preceding 12 months (or the shorter required period); (iii) those reports include the third party's financial statements; and (iv) if incorporated into a prospectus/registration statement, the prospectus must state that all subsequent documents filed by such third party prior to termination of the offering will also be deemed incorporated. Instructions address compliance with Commission rules on incorporation by reference (e.g., Reg S-T Rule 303), filings undertakings (Item 512 of Reg S-K), knowledge qualifications when no relationship exists, special definition of 'financial statements' for asset-backed issuers, and other procedural conditions. Also provides reference-information alternative for significant obligors subject to additional eligibility criteria (paragraph (c)(2) conditions (i) and (ii)(A)-(F)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 1100(d) Other participants and pool assets representing interests in other asset pools
rubrics_metrics.description: If an ABS transaction involves additional or intermediate parties not specifically identified in Regulation AB, disclose material information regarding any such party and its role, function and experience in relation to the ABS and the asset pool and describe material terms of any agreement with such party and file such agreement as an exhibit. If the asset pool includes pool assets representing an interest in or right to payments of another asset pool, references to the asset pool and the pool assets of the issuing entity also include the other asset pool and its pool assets if specified conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions for including another asset pool include: (i) both issuing entity and entity issuing the included pool asset were established under direction of the same sponsor or depositor; and (ii) the pool asset was created solely to satisfy legal requirements or otherwise facilitate structuring. Instruction: reference to the underlying asset pool includes compliance with applicable servicing criteria and the servicer compliance statement required by Item 1123; provide clear and concise disclosure, including flow charts or other illustrations, of the transaction and the various parties involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 1100(e) Foreign asset-backed securities
rubrics_metrics.description: If ABS are issued by a foreign issuer, backed by foreign assets, or affected by enhancement/support provided by a foreign entity, the filing must describe any pertinent governmental, legal, regulatory or administrative matters and any pertinent tax matters, exchange controls, currency restrictions or other economic, fiscal, monetary or potential factors in the applicable home jurisdiction that could materially affect payments on, the performance of, or other matters relating to, the assets in the pool or the ABS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also: in a Securities Act registration statement provide the information required by Item 101(g) of Regulation S-K. Disclosure is also required in Forms 10-D and 10-K with respect to the ABS regarding any material impact caused by foreign legal and regulatory developments during the period covered by the report that have not been previously described in a Form 10-D, 10-K or 8-K. See Instruction 2 to Item 202 of Regulation S-K for related guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 1100(f) Filing of required exhibits (Regulation AB)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where agreements or other documents in Regulation AB are specified to be filed as exhibits to a Securities Act registration statement, such agreements or other documents, if applicable, may be incorporated by reference as an exhibit to the registration statement (e.g., by filing a Form 8-K). Final agreements must be filed and made part of the registration statement no later than the date the final prospectus is required to be filed under § 230.424 of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: incorporation by reference as an exhibit by filing a Form 8-K in the case of offerings registered on Form SF-3. Emphasizes timing for final agreements and applicability to registration statements/prospectuses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 1101 ABS informational and computational material (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines 'ABS informational and computational material' as a written communication consisting solely of one or some combination of: (1) factual information regarding the ABS being offered and the structure/basic parameters of the securities (e.g., number of classes, seniority, payment priorities, terms of payment, tax/ERISA/legal conclusions of counsel, descriptive info on each class such as principal amount, coupon, anticipated price, yield, weighted average life, credit enhancements, anticipated ratings); (2) factual information regarding the pool assets underlying the ABS (origination, acquisition, pool selection criteria, prefunding/revolving period info, significant obligors, contractual characteristics such as weighted average coupon/maturity, delinquency/loss info and geographic distribution); (3) identification of key parties to the transaction (servicers, trustees, depositors, sponsors, originators, providers of enhancement/support) with brief description of each party's roles, responsibilities, background and experience; (4) static pool data (as referenced in Item 1105) for sponsor's/servicer's portfolio, prior transactions or the asset pool; and (5) statistical information displaying for a class of ABS the yield, average life, expected maturity, interest rate sensitivity, cash flow characteristics, total rate of return, option adjusted spread or other financial/statistical information under specified hypothetical prepayment, interest rate, loss or other scenarios.
